analysis: The only change in this PR is in .github/workflows/ci.yml. It adds one step to the release-integrity job, after line 148 at head lines 149-155: 'Refuse back-deployed Date comparisons in provider source'. The step runs three local Python scripts: scripts/test-check-date-comparisons.py, scripts/test-check-provider-weak-imports.py and scripts/check-date-comparisons.py. It adds no secrets, no new permissions (the workflow keeps contents: read), no network access, no new third-party actions and no changed triggers. Cache handling, runner routing and artifact uploads are unchanged. The step is a read-only static check of provider source, and it narrows the build-quality gate rather than widening any trust boundary. I found no effect on the threat-model assets or boundaries: provider keys, the attestation chain (TB-009), the App Attest authorization (TB-011), the prefix cache (T-041), and the coordinator-provider WebSocket (TB-002). Unverified: the contents of the three new scripts are not in the supplied evidence. Whether they are robust, or whether they could fail open and silently skip checks, was not examined. That affects CI hygiene only, not a production security conclusion. The workflow's reliance on script exit codes is the only relevant contract. I don't see evidence of a security regression, so there are no findings.
